49.0.0.en: The prophet Jeremiah marvels at the enmity of the children of Ammon toward the children of Israel. The tribe of Gad dwelt east of the river Jordan, where the kingdom of the children of Ammon lies, north of the kingdom of Moab. The children of Ammon were distinguished by enmity toward the people of God throughout the generations, from the days of the judges until near the birth of Christ. So Jeremiah grieves that the king of the children of Ammon advanced and seized some of the land of the tribe of Gad, that is, of the people of God. In some translations “Malcham” is written instead of “their king”, and Malcham is the god of the children of Ammon, to whom human sacrifices were offered; what is meant is that the people of the children of Ammon seize and dwell in the cities of the children of Israel.

49.1.0.en: Rabbah of the children of Ammon: the capital of the children of Ammon, which is now Amman, the capital of Jordan.

49.1.1.en: Because of the enmity of the children of Ammon toward the people of God, God chastens them by means of Babylon, so the noise of war is heard in their capital Rabbah. The army of Babylon makes Rabbah known as a heap, and they burn her daughters with fire, that is, they kill the inhabitants of Rabbah. What is meant by Israel’s inheriting those who were his heirs is Babylon’s seizing their cities; that is, God chastens the enemies of the people of God.

49.2.0.en: Ai: either a Moabite city or a word meaning destruction, and what is meant is the destruction of the cities of the children of Ammon.

49.2.1.en: Heshbon: the capital of Moab, which was mostly in the possession of Moab and sometimes in the possession of the children of Ammon. Jeremiah calls to it to weep over the city of Ai, which belonged to the children of Ammon. He also calls the women of the city of Rabbah, the capital of the children of Ammon, to cry out in sorrow over their slain, and asks them to put on coarse clothes such as sackcloth, as a sign of great grief; they used to wear it especially on the middle and below, that is, the loins. Then they utter words of lament, that is, wailing, for the ruin that came upon them, and they also run to and fro among the walls of the temples seeking the help of the gods, but there is no helper, because the Babylonian captivity has taken the king, the priests and the leaders, and the remaining people of the children of Ammon are in great humiliation.

49.3.0.en: Valleys: the valleys. The people of the children of Ammon boasted of their fertile plains, which gave good crops and many good things, so the prophet calls on them to cease their boasting, after the valleys were filled with the blood of their slain, because of their turning away from God, their worship of idols, and their reliance on their wealth and good things, which will be destroyed at the hand of Babylon.

49.4.0.en: When the army of Babylon attacks the inhabitants of the children of Ammon, it fills their hearts with fear and they flee, leaving their lands, and Babylon takes their men captive and moves them to other distant lands. In the end the land of the children of Ammon is emptied of its inhabitants and its people are scattered in many lands, and they are unable to return and gather again in their land.

49.4.1.en: (v. 6): Jeremiah gives them the good news that they will return from captivity. The book of Nehemiah tells us that Tobiah the Ammonite was a leader of the children of Ammon, and that was during the captivity of Media and Persia. This verse is also a prophecy of the return of the children of Ammon to the faith, that is, their faith as Gentiles in Christ, for Christ came for the sake of the Jews and the Gentiles.

49.4.2.en: Do not rely on your wealth and good things, for they are changeable, but rely on God, the Giver of these good things, and thank Him every day for His kindnesses. He gave them to you as proof of His love, so that your heart may cling to Him, to set out in prayers, meditations and service to Him.

49.4.4.en: 7- Concerning Edom, thus saith the LORD of hosts; Is wisdom no more in Teman? is counsel perished from the prudent? is their wisdom vanished? 8- Flee ye, turn back, dwell deep, O inhabitants of Dedan; for I will bring the calamity of Esau upon him, the time that I will visit him. 9- If grapegatherers come to thee, would they not leave some gleaning grapes? if thieves by night, they will destroy till they have enough. 10- But I have made Esau bare, I have uncovered his secret places, and he shall not be able to hide himself: his seed is spoiled, and his brethren, and his neighbours, and he is not. 11- Leave thy fatherless children, I will preserve them alive; and let thy widows trust in me. 12- For thus saith the LORD; Behold, they whose judgment was not to drink of the cup have assuredly drunken; and art thou he that shall altogether go unpunished? thou shalt not go unpunished, but thou shalt surely drink of it. 13- For I have sworn by myself, saith the LORD, that Bozrah shall become a desolation, a reproach, a waste, and a curse; and all the cities thereof shall be perpetual wastes. 14- I have heard a rumour from the LORD, and an ambassador is sent unto the heathen, saying, Gather ye together, and come against her, and rise up to the battle. 15- For, lo, I will make thee small among the heathen, and despised among men.

49.4.5.en: 16- Thy terribleness hath deceived thee, and the pride of thine heart, O thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, that holdest the height of the hill: though thou shouldest make thy nest as high as the eagle, I will bring thee down from thence, saith the LORD. 17- Also Edom shall be a desolation: every one that goeth by it shall be astonished, and shall hiss at all the plagues thereof. 18- As in the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah and the neighbour cities thereof, saith the LORD, no man shall abide there, neither shall a son of man dwell in it. 19- Behold, he shall come up like a lion from the swelling of Jordan against the habitation of the strong: but I will suddenly make him run away from her: and who is a chosen man, that I may appoint over her? for who is like me? and who will appoint me the time? and who is that shepherd that will stand before me? 20- Therefore hear the counsel of the LORD, that he hath taken against Edom; and his purposes, that he hath purposed against the inhabitants of Teman: Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out: surely he shall make their habitations desolate with them. 21- The earth is moved at the noise of their fall, at the cry the noise thereof was heard in the Red sea. 22- Behold, he shall come up and fly as the eagle, and spread his wings over Bozrah: and at that day shall the heart of the mighty men of Edom be as the heart of a woman in her pangs.

49.5.0.en: Edom: this is Esau, and the word Edom means red. He dwelt in the mountains of Seir, which lie south of Palestine, and its capital was Sela. It resisted the children of Israel greatly and sometimes submitted to them, and King Herod in the days of Christ was an Edomite.

49.6.0.en: Teman: its meaning is the south. It is one of the most important cities of the Edomites and was named after a grandson of Esau; it lies north-east of the land of Edom, and its people were distinguished by wisdom and the speaking of proverbs.

49.6.1.en: Jeremiah marvels at the fall of Teman and the land of Edom at the hand of the Babylonians, and asks where their wisdom is, which did not help them to defend themselves before Babylon.

49.7.0.en: Dedan: a son of Abraham by Keturah; he dwelt south-east of Edom and was subject to it, and his people were distinguished by trade.

49.7.1.en: Dwell deep: hide. He calls the land of Dedan, which was subject to Edom and neighboring it, to flee and look right and left as they flee for fear of the Babylonian enemies, and to hide as far as they can, because God’s wrath on Edom has come upon them also.

49.8.0.en: Gleaning grapes: the few fruits remaining on the cluster of grapes or on the branches of the tree.

49.8.1.en: The prophet is astonished at Babylon’s destruction of the land of the Edomites, because it is customary that the grapegatherers, when they gather the fruits, leave some berries or a few fruits, and thieves, when they steal, take what suffices them and leave the rest, but Babylon shattered Edom completely.

49.9.0.en: This is what happened to Edom at the hand of Babylon: complete destruction of his seed, his brethren and his neighbors, that is, all his inhabitants and those of the neighboring peoples on whom he relies. The enemy left nothing of the possessions of Edom without seizing and shattering it, so Edom was completely stripped, and nothing precious was left to him hidden or concealed.

49.10.0.en: God turns back and gives hope to Edom, that after the killing of its men He will call and preserve its orphan children and its widowed women. For God does not intend the destruction of the nations but their return to Him by faith and repentance when they hear Jeremiah’s prophecies about them, and also when some of them die and the rest believe.

49.11.0.en: What is meant by the cup is the cup of divine wrath, and those whose judgment was not to drink of the cup are the people of God. That is, if God has allowed His people to be chastened for their sins so that they repent, then all the more the wicked Edom, which worships idols and is proud, ought to drink the cup of God’s wrath, because the just God judges him and does not acquit him.

49.12.0.en: Bozrah: a main city in Edom, which was for some time its capital.

49.12.1.en: God declares the destruction of the most important city of Edom, Bozrah, so that whoever passes by it is astonished at its ruin after it was a great city; it becomes a proverb of reproach and curse, because it does not rise or get built again.

49.13.0.en: God shows what will happen to Edom, which is the gathering of the nations, that is, the armies of Babylon, against it to destroy it.

49.14.0.en: After Edom’s destruction it does not remain a strong people but becomes small and despised among the peoples.

49.15.0.en: The clefts of the rock: caves among the rocks, in which the Edomites used to dwell, fortified in the rocks, in hiding places where they felt that no one could reach them because of their strength.

49.15.1.en: The hill: the mound or plateau. He rebukes Edom for its pride and its terrifying the peoples around it, because it is strong and dwells above the mountains in fortified caves, and God says to it that if you liken yourself to the eagle, the strongest of the birds of prey, which cannot be reached, God by His power brings it down to the ground and destroys its land at the hand of Babylon.

49.16.0.en: Because of the destruction of Edom, which was a great country, everyone who passes by it marvels, and even hisses in mockery of it because of its ruin.

49.17.0.en: He likens the destruction of Edom to the ruin of Sodom and Gomorrah and the neighboring cities, that is, a total destruction, so that no man can dwell there but it becomes completely deserted.

49.18.0.en: The swelling of Jordan: the waters of the river Jordan when they overflow with force and pride. He likens the army of Babylon, in its attack on Edom, to the lion, the king of the beasts in his strength, and likens it also to the flood of the waters of the Jordan, which attacks Edom, which was fertile pastures. But God winks at it, that is, signals to it, so it turns back from Edom and does not kill everyone in it, so it runs away from it, that is, Babylon runs and moves away from Edom. Then God speaks with power, describing Himself as the shepherd who has full authority over all the earth, so He commands Babylon and it attacks Edom, and then He stops it and turns it back from it, because God is the Ruler of all.

49.19.0.en: God declares His judgment on the land of Edom, one of whose most famous cities is Teman, that it will become very weak after the Babylonian attack, so that flocks of weak sheep drag them away after the destruction of its cities.

49.20.0.en: He shows the extent of Edom’s calamity and the cry of its sorrowing people: from the violence of the Babylonian attack they will cry out so loudly that their voice is heard in the Red Sea, and so their cry reaches Egypt, and all the lands of the peoples around Edom tremble and shake because of its calamity.

49.21.0.en: He likens the army of Babylon to the strong eagle that spreads its wings over the land of Edom, that is, attacks it and destroys its cities, symbolized by Bozrah, its capital, and no strong man remains to defend Edom, but its mighty ones become weak and in pain like a woman when she gives birth.

49.21.1.en: If pride is the cause of many evils and brings God’s wrath, then humility is the shortest way to the heart of God. So declare your repentance before Him and plead with Him in reverence, and you will obtain mercies; your true humility appears when you humble yourself and bear with those around you.

49.21.3.en: 23- Concerning Damascus. Hamath is confounded, and Arpad: for they have heard evil tidings: they are fainthearted; there is sorrow on the sea; it cannot be quiet. 24- Damascus is waxed feeble, and turneth herself to flee, and fear hath seized on her: anguish and sorrows have taken her, as a woman in travail. 25- How is the city of praise not left, the city of my joy! 26- Therefore her young men shall fall in her streets, and all the men of war shall be cut off in that day, saith the LORD of hosts. 27- And I will kindle a fire in the wall of Damascus, and it shall consume the palaces of Benhadad.

49.22.0.en: Damascus: the capital of the land of the Arameans, that is, Syria; it is an ancient and strong city. Hamath and Arpad: great Syrian lands that come after Damascus in Aram, which is Syria. When the land of the Arameans heard the news of the Babylonian attack, it was very afraid and fell into shame, because of its weakness before the power of the enemies, and was troubled like the raging sea.

49.23.0.en: Damascus and the lands around it were alarmed and became terrified before Babylon, in pain like a woman when she gives birth.

49.24.0.en: Damascus was distinguished by corruption and the pleasures of various lusts, but all this joy was lost by Babylon’s attack on it and the killing of its young men and all its men of war.

49.25.0.en: Benhadad: a title of the kings of Damascus.

49.25.1.en: The city of Damascus shelters behind its high walls, but when Babylon attacks it, its walls are burned, a sign of its ruin.

49.25.2.en: The pleasure of sin is temporary, but the pleasure of virtue is lasting. So hold fast to the love of God and delight in fellowship with Him, so that your peace and joy endure and the devil, the enemy, cannot shatter you.

49.25.4.en: 28- Concerning Kedar, and concerning the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon shall smite, thus saith the LORD; Arise ye, go up to Kedar, and spoil the men of the east. 29- Their tents and their flocks shall they take away: they shall take to themselves their curtains, and all their vessels, and their camels; and they shall cry unto them, Fear is on every side. 30- Flee, get you far off, dwell deep, O ye inhabitants of Hazor, saith the LORD; for Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon hath taken counsel against you, and hath conceived a purpose against you. 31- Arise, get you up unto the wealthy nation, that dwelleth without care, saith the LORD, which have neither gates nor bars, which dwell alone. 32- And their camels shall be a booty, and the multitude of their cattle a spoil: and I will scatter into all winds them that are in the utmost corners; and I will bring their calamity from all sides thereof, saith the LORD. 33- And Hazor shall be a dwelling for dragons, and a desolation for ever: there shall no man abide there, nor any son of man dwell in it.

49.26.0.en: Kedar: the most famous of the tribes of the land of Arabia; the word means black. They dwell in tents and not in cities, that is, they are Bedouin, and they owned many cattle and were rich. Hazor: lies south of the Euphrates, that is, in the north of the Arabian Peninsula; they are Bedouin tribes who dwell in tents or in unwalled villages.

49.26.1.en: Jeremiah’s prophecy calls the armies of Babylon to attack the tribes of Kedar, who dwell in the east of Egypt.

49.27.0.en: Curtains: pieces of cloth attached to the tents to enlarge them.

49.27.1.en: When Babylon attacks Kedar, it seizes their tents, their sheep, their curtains and their vessels, so the inhabitants of Kedar are afraid and try to flee, for they feel the Babylonian attack besieging them from every side. Babylon did not take them captive, feeling that it had no need of them, and was content to plunder their possessions.

49.28.0.en: Likewise the tribes of Hazor feared because of the command of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to attack them, and from their fear they tried to flee to escape from his hand and to hide, after they felt their defeat and weakness before him.

49.29.0.en: Those that are in the utmost corners (with the hair cut round): they used to please their gods by cutting their hair round, leaving some hair on top of their heads, and what is meant here is the people of Hazor.

49.29.1.en: The tribes of Hazor were rich in many cattle and camels, so the Babylonians plundered them and their inhabitants, with their hair cut round, fled, and the Babylonians killed many of them, and thus they were scattered as the farmer scatters the chaff with the winnowing fork, that is, it flies in the air.

49.30.0.en: Dragons (jackals): a predatory animal whose size is between the fox and the wolf, which lives in deserted places.

49.30.1.en: The land of Hazor becomes a ruin in which people do not dwell but the animals that live in deserted places, such as jackals.

49.30.2.en: Do not resemble the people of the world in appearance, and let your trust be in God and not in the multitude of your material possessions. In proportion to your care, you will enjoy a pure relationship with God and experience His love. [5] Elam (vv. 34-39:)

49.30.3.en: 34- The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet against Elam in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, saying, 35- Thus saith the LORD of hosts; Behold, I will break the bow of Elam, the chief of their might. 36- And upon Elam will I bring the four winds from the four quarters of heaven, and will scatter them toward all those winds; and there shall be no nation whither the outcasts of Elam shall not come. 37- For I will cause Elam to be dismayed before their enemies, and before them that seek their life: and I will bring evil upon them, even my fierce anger, saith the LORD; and I will send the sword after them, till I have consumed them: 38- And I will set my throne in Elam, and will destroy from thence the king and the princes, saith the LORD. 39- But it shall come to pass in the latter days, that I will bring again the captivity of Elam, saith the LORD.

49.31.0.en: Elam: a strong country lying east of Babylon, distinguished by shooting arrows. It submitted to Assyria and then Babylon, but its strength afterward helped in shattering Babylon and the rise of the kingdom of Media and Persia. The time of this prophecy is fixed as the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah, the last of the kings of Judah.

49.32.0.en: God declares the defeat of Elam before Babylon and the shattering of their power, which appears in their skill in shooting arrows with the bow.

49.33.0.en: When Babylon attacks Elam, it attacks them from every side and drives out its inhabitants, and they are scattered over the whole earth as the farmer scatters the chaff, so that it flies in the air in every place.

49.34.0.en: The Elamites become very afraid, and Babylon kills many of them.

49.35.0.en: God sets His throne in Elam, and what is meant by this is Babylon’s dominion over them, because Babylon is the divine instrument in chastening the nations, and God destroys the king and the princes of Elam.

49.36.0.en: God gives hope to Elam of a return from captivity, not only after the fall of Babylon but also through the faith of the Elamites in Christ. They are mentioned in the second chapter of the book of Acts as being gathered in Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost, and they believed in Christ.

49.36.1.en: Some may think that their bodily strength, their material weapons, the various powers of the world and their possessions may give them success. But let your strength be spiritual, that is, your faith in Christ, who is able to overcome the world, so that you are not troubled by all its changes.
